title: Quotient squares for normalized finite open scalar maps
statement: Fix the actual coefficient and open interfaces of [def-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model-data], supplied Operations o and quotient-compatible OrdinaryReductions AX and AU. Assume that o.openSystems.restrictionEvaluation is identity on underlying sections, and supply any generator-normalized finite TensorComparison tc. Define scalarLevelComparison by composing AX.evaluation, tc.ordinary, inverse AU.evaluation and inverse extensionEvaluation. For every module M and every n≤m, these component maps commute with the actual semilinear quotient transition: transition_source followed by scalar restriction of the level-n map equals the level-m map followed by transition_target. No existence of a finite comparison, of a strict-system map, or of a strict-system isomorphism is asserted.

proof.text: Define reductionUnit using the native finite scalar-unit section and inverse OrdinaryReduction evaluation. Reuse the proved generic transportedUnitLaw and quotient_mate_law in the proof module of [stage3-pur-extension-quotient-unit-successor], which are stated for an arbitrary n≤m. Specialize them to OrdinaryReduction.quotient to prove horizontal compatibility of reductionUnit. The section specifications of the two transition interfaces identify both with the same horizontal presheaf map.

Use the proved section calculus [lem-sf-open-system-unit-sections]: transport a sequence section and apply the open-system unit; presheaf naturality gives horizontal compatibility, and unit_evaluation together with identity restrictionEvaluation identifies its finite evaluation with finiteExtensionSection.

On reductionUnit of each original completed extension generator, expand scalarLevelComparison, cancel the evaluation isomorphisms, and apply tc.generators. Naturality of finite extension on summands and the preceding evaluation identity identify its image with systemUnit of the slice reductionUnit. Therefore both transition composites agree on those generators by the two horizontal compatibility equations. Precompose with inverse AX evaluation and use injectivity of the scalar adjunction Hom equivalence. Use injectivity of the localized completed extension Hom equivalence, the prescribed summand unit and invertibility of the integral transport to reduce equality to the generator equations. Cancel inverse AX evaluation. This proves the displayed morphism equality for arbitrary n≤m, including identity transitions and the empty open.
